new-profiles-audit.json.method: Official OCA ecclesiastical biographies were retrieved with web browsing. Exact page titles, specific locators, supported facts, and caveats are recorded below. Calendar dates are raw ecclesiastical dates, not converted civil dates.

entries.result: Official ecclesiastical source retrieved; name and fixed commemoration verified
evidence: OCA title and commemoration label: November 19.
Birth and formation; consecration in 1817; metropolitan rank in 1826; catechism dated 1823; death November 19, 1867.
issuesOrOmissions: OCA article gives glorification as 1995; other references give 1994. Glorification year omitted pending comparison with the Russian Church act.
Birth/death dates are retained as printed by the ecclesiastical source; no historical Julian-to-Gregorian conversion is asserted.

entries.result: Official ecclesiastical source retrieved; name and fixed commemoration verified
evidence: OCA full ecclesiastical biography identifies the Serbian hierarch, 1881 birth, episcopate, wartime imprisonment, American ministry and 1956 death.
issuesOrOmissions: OCA supplementary calendar gives March 18 and April 20 as ecclesiastical commemorations. These are calendar dates before the app’s selected-calendar civil conversion.
The source’s detailed wartime claims and education claims were not expanded beyond the facts needed for identification; academic degree details and liberation chronology omitted.

entries.evidence: OCA lists March 18 (repose), April 20 (translation of relics), and glorification May 19, 2003.

entries.result: Official ecclesiastical source retrieved; name and fixed commemoration verified
evidence: Birth 1731, episcopal appointment 1764, Athos 1777, final Chios residence 1790–1805, death April 17, 1805, recovery of relics 1808.
issuesOrOmissions: Reason for his replacement at Corinth is uncertain even in the source’s footnote; no definitive motive asserted.
The biography describes his connection with New Martyrs; it does not make Makarios himself a martyr.

entries.result: Official ecclesiastical source retrieved; name and fixed commemoration verified
evidence: OCA biography identifies Naxos, 1748, Dionysiou, Philokalia collaboration, Great Schema 1783, publications, repose July 14, 1809, glorification 1955.
issuesOrOmissions: Birth year 1748 follows OCA. Other reference traditions use 1749, so the date label identifies the source chronology.
A source sentence calls the seven Catholic Epistles Saint Paul’s; that apparent error is not repeated.
The source year 4465 appears only in the calendar route, not as a publication date or historical claim.

entries.result: Official ecclesiastical source retrieved; name and fixed commemoration verified
evidence: Opening birth range, first chronicle mention 1405, Vladimir 1408, Trinity icon, death range 1427–1430 and Andronikov burial.
issuesOrOmissions: OCA also says he was over seventy at death; this is not reconciled with its approximate birth/death ranges, so that age is omitted.
No plague cause or precise January death date asserted from unsourced reference lists.

entries.result: Official ecclesiastical source retrieved; name and fixed commemoration verified
evidence: The entry under August 17 is explicitly for Alypios the iconographer of the Kiev Near Caves, not Alypius of Tagaste or a modern Russian painter.
Greek teachers 1083, priest-monk, charity, traditional miracles, repose 1114, burial, September 28 and second Sunday of Great Lent.
issuesOrOmissions: Miraculous details are explicitly attributed to the ecclesiastical life and not presented as independently documented historical events.
The URL’s year 9999 is an OCA calendar-route value; it is not the date of the events or a publication date.

entries.result: Official ecclesiastical source retrieved; name and fixed commemoration verified
evidence: Heading: May 21; title Equal of the Apostles; son of Constantius and Helena, York accession 306, Milan 313, Council 325, Baptism and death 337.
issuesOrOmissions: Precise birth year omitted because the ecclesiastical source gives 274 whereas historical references vary.
The source’s reported Cross vision retains explicit attribution; political actions do not make every action of his reign a doctrinal ruling.
No modern ecclesiastical worship directions are inferred from the narrative.

entries.result: Named Orthodox Saint and ecclesiastical commemoration verified in the sources
supportedEvidence: OCA title explicitly names the fool-for-Christ at Constantinople; feast October 2; Slav; traditional tenth century and death936; Blachernae vision and Protection feast.
issuesOrOmissions: Chronology follows the liturgical biography; no independent historical certainty is claimed for the hagiographic episodes.
No imitation of this exceptional ascetic life is presented as a prayer rule or beginner instruction.

entries.result: Named Orthodox Saint and ecclesiastical commemoration verified in the sources
supportedEvidence: Official Russian Synodal Department publication gives5/18May, unknown origins, Alexis relationship, founding narrative, peaceful May5,1377repose.
OCA calendar confirmsMay5 but supplies no biography.
issuesOrOmissions: Dates in the late founding tradition have been questioned by ecclesiastical reference scholarship; this profile labels them traditional.
The story’s speculative journeys with Alexis and hypothetical monastic rules are not asserted as facts.

entries.result: Named Orthodox Saint and ecclesiastical commemoration verified in the sources
supportedEvidence: OCA title identifies Bishop of Ryazan; July3andJune10commemorations;1295repose;1609uncovering; Laurentian Chronicle; mantle miracle is tradition.
issuesOrOmissions: Miraculous travel is explicitly attributed to the ecclesiastical life.
Not conflated with Basil of RyazanII or Basil of Ancyra.

entries.result: Named Orthodox Saint and ecclesiastical commemoration verified in the sources
supportedEvidence: OCA biography of his son identifies the elder Basil as lawyer/rhetorician, father of ten and initial educator.
Antiochian-hosted sheet explicitly gives Saint title and Greek May30commemoration.
issuesOrOmissions: The Antiochian sheet is a permitted republication from OrthodoxWiki; the official host confirms ecclesiastical reception, not a newly discovered ancient biography.
No birthdate, deathyear350, episcopal office, ordination, written treatise, or invented martyrdom added.
The Antiochian sheet’s January3phrase concerns Emilia and is not used to assign that feast to Basil the Elder.

entries.result: Named Orthodox Saint and ecclesiastical commemoration verified in the sources
supportedEvidence: OCA Orthodox calendarMarch14;480birth; Subiaco; communities; Monte Cassino; Rule;547repose and GregoryDialogues.
issuesOrOmissions: No claim that he invented all Western monasticism; he was an influential organizer and Rule writer.
Later Roman Catholic observances are not substituted for the OrthodoxMarch14feast.

entries.result: Named Orthodox Saint and ecclesiastical commemoration verified in the sources
supportedEvidence: OCA Saint life: March11; Damascus c560; monastic travel; JohnMoschus; writings; Jerusalem siege.
issuesOrOmissions: There is an internal OCA source discrepancy: the Saint life gives634–644, while Church History gives634–638. Dates here explicitly follow Church History.
The app does not present all traditional literary attributions as established modern authorship.
No claim that Sophronius attended the Sixth Council, which occurred after his death.

entries.result: Named Orthodox Saint and ecclesiastical commemoration verified in the sources
supportedEvidence: Named OCA December21entry: Volhynia; monk; iconographer; Rata monastery; metropolitan;Moscow1325;death1326;veneration1339.
issuesOrOmissions: The OCA life contains complicated chronology around his appointment; exact consecration year omitted.
Residence transfer is described in readable terms without claiming that the historical metropolitan title immediately became Moscow in every usage.

entries.result: Named Orthodox Saint and ecclesiastical commemoration verified in the sources
supportedEvidence: OCA history explicitly titles him Saint Peter Mogila; school,1632selection,1640and1642councils, criticism of Latin influence and recognition by Churches.
Romanian Patriarchate agency gives December22calendar, Suceava family, death and Kiev Cavesburial.
issuesOrOmissions: Commemoration follows the verified Romanian Patriarchate December22record. Other local Church calendars differ; the app must not claim a universally identical feast.
OCA and Romanian paragraphs partly overlap, so all biography paraphrase words are kept concise even across sources.
No role as an Ecumenical Council father is asserted.

wholeAppBudgetRevision.note: Shortened this source-derived profile prose; no source references reassigned and Romanian calendar material unchanged. Existing app and timeline files were not changed.

Greek calendars also commemorate himFebruary16; this profile’s main feast followsOCAFebruary18.
Not confused with Flavian of Antioch.
